Steaks

Excision
of

visceral
organs
was
necessary
once

viscera
had
been
exposed

in
steaking .
The
stomach
was
emptied ,
and
the
heart ,
liver ,
gall
bladder ,
pylorus ,

pancreas ,
spleen ,
spiral
valve ,
and
rectal
gland
were
weighed
individually
using
an

Ohaus
balance
( table
3 ) .
The
suprahepatic
rete
was
usually
excised
last ,
both
lobes

at
once .

The
kidney
could
be
found
by
first
removing
the
claspers
( in
the
case
of
the

male )
and
anal
fins ,
and
then
finding
where
the
lower
lateral
cutaneous
arteries
( at

the
level
of
the
cloaca )
converged
into
the
cloacal
arteries
and
turned
sharply

toward
the
ventral
midline
( figure
10 ) .
Just
under
the
ureter ,
these
cloacal
arteries

enter
the
posterior
lobe
of
the
sub - renal
rete
( figure
11
) ,
which
comprises
the

posterior - most
point
of
the
kidney
on
the
ventral
side .
The
entire
kidney

excised

weighing
and
study
of
the
rete

12 ) .

After
weights

taken ,

suprahepatic
retial

9 ) ,

of

posterior
lobe
of
the
sub - renal
rete

( figure
13 )
and
the
muscle
rete

4 ) ,

be
viewed
under
the
dissecting
scope .

micrometry

diameters

Leica
MZ8

6x
